Question: Why must <meta charset="UTF-8"> be placed within the first 1024 bytes of an HTML document?
Answer: HTML is streamed over the network as raw binary bytes. If the encoding tag is missing or placed late, the browser must guess the encoding and start tokenizing. Discovering charset="UTF-8" later forces the browser to discard the partially built DOM tree and restart parsing from scratch, introducing major performance lag.

Question: What happens if you omit <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0"> on mobile devices?
Answer: Mobile browsers assume the page is built for desktop and render it on an artificial 980px virtual canvas, scaling it down so text and touch targets become microscopic. The viewport meta tag forces the CSS layout width to match the physical device width in CSS pixels at a 1:1 initial scale.

Question: How does <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin> accelerate font loading?
Answer: It performs DNS resolution, TCP 3-way handshake, and TLS cryptographic negotiation with the third-party server during early HTML parsing before the font file is even requested in CSS, cutting 100ms-300ms off download latency. crossorigin is required because fonts are fetched via CORS.

Question: What is the difference between FOIT and FOUT, and how does display=swap resolve it?
Answer: FOIT (Flash of Invisible Text) hides text for up to 3 seconds while waiting for custom web fonts to download, showing blank whitespace. FOUT (Flash of Unstyled Text) renders a system fallback font immediately. display=swap enforces a 0-second block period and infinite swap period, ensuring text is instantly readable and smoothly swapped when the web font arrives.

Question: Why is <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css"> render-blocking by default in modern browsers?
Answer: The browser intentionally halts constructing the Render Tree and painting pixels until the stylesheet is downloaded and parsed into the CSSOM. This prevents FOUC (Flash of Unstyled Content), guaranteeing the user never sees raw unstyled markup before styles apply.

Question: What is the primary accessibility (a11y) role of the <title> tag?
Answer: The <title> tag is the very first piece of information read aloud by screen readers (NVDA, VoiceOver, JAWS) upon page load or tab switching, providing essential orientation context to visually impaired users before they begin navigating landmarks.

Question: Why is the crossorigin attribute required on <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>?
Answer: Web font files (.woff2) are fetched using anonymous Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS). Without the crossorigin attribute, the browser establishes a credentials-carrying connection that cannot be reused for anonymous font requests, rendering the preconnect hint useless.

Question: What is the purpose of <meta name="description" content="...">?
Answer: It provides a 150-160 character summary used by search engine crawlers (Googlebot, Bing) for SERP snippet descriptions and by social media link preview generators when the webpage URL is shared.
